Load a Ligand-Receptor Pair Database

Source: R/load_LRM_database.R
load_LRM_database.Rd

Returns a standardized ligand-receptor pair table for use as the LRM.db argument of create_NICHESObject() and compute_CellToCell(). Two curated databases can be loaded by name; alternatively, any user-supplied data.frame is accepted and column names are remapped to the canonical "ligand" / "receptor" names.

Usage

load_LRM_database(
  db = "connectomedb2025",
  species = "human",
  ligand.col = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

db

Character string ("connectomedb2025" (default), "fantom5", or "omnipath") OR a data.frame / data.table with at least two columns containing ligand and receptor gene symbols.

species

Species for built-in databases. One of "human" (default), "mouse", "rat", or "pig" (ConnectomeDB2025 and FANTOM5 only; OmniPath does not support pig). Ignored silently when db is a data.frame.

ligand.col

Column name for ligand symbols when db is a data.frame. Default: "ligand".

receptor.col

Column name for receptor symbols when db is a data.frame. Default: "receptor".

verbose

Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A data.frame with columns "ligand", "receptor", and any additional annotation columns present in the source. Rows with NA in ligand or receptor are silently removed.

Built-in databases

"connectomedb2025"

ConnectomeDB2025 ligand-receptor pairs (default), bundled within the package for human, mouse, rat, and pig. No internet access or additional packages required. Includes experimentally verified and orthology-inferred interactions with evidence labels and subcellular location annotations.

"fantom5"

Ramilowski et al. (2015) FANTOM5 ligand-receptor pairs, bundled within the package for human, mouse, rat, and pig. No internet access or additional packages required. Species-specific datasets were derived using the methodology in Raredon et al. 2019 (DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aaw3851).

"omnipath"

OmniPath ligand-receptor extra interactions (Turei et al. 2021). Requires internet access and the OmnipathR package. Install with: BiocManager::install("OmnipathR"). Supported species: "human", "mouse", "rat".

Complex ligands/receptors

Both built-in databases and user-supplied tables may contain gene complexes. Complexes are represented as underscore-joined gene symbols, e.g. "COL1A1_COL1A2" for the collagen I heterodimer. The scoring functions in NICHESv2 handle complexes automatically.

Examples

# ConnectomeDB2025 is the default -- no db argument needed.
# \donttest{
lrm.human <- load_LRM_database(species = "human")
#> [load_LRM_database] Loading ConnectomeDB2025 (human) from bundled package data ...
#> [load_LRM_database] ConnectomeDB2025 (human): 3550 unique LR pairs loaded.
head(lrm.human)
#>   ligand receptor interaction.id      lr.pair evidence         ligand.location
#> 1    A2M     LRP1  CDB15:0000001     A2M LRP1   Direct                secreted
#> 2    ACE   BDKRB2  CDB15:0000002   ACE BDKRB2   Direct secreted, cell membrane
#> 3 ADAM10    EPHA3  CDB15:0000003 ADAM10 EPHA3   Direct           cell membrane
#> 4 ADAM12    ITGA9  CDB15:0000004 ADAM12 ITGA9   Direct secreted, cell membrane
#> 5 ADAM12    ITGB1  CDB15:0000005 ADAM12 ITGB1   Direct secreted, cell membrane
#> 6 ADAM12     SDC4  CDB15:0000006  ADAM12 SDC4 Inferred secreted, cell membrane
#>   receptor.location
#> 1     cell membrane
#> 2     cell membrane
#> 3     cell membrane
#> 4     cell membrane
#> 5     cell membrane
#> 6     cell membrane

# FANTOM5 -- bundled, always available, no internet.
lrm.f5  <- load_LRM_database("fantom5", species = "human")
#> [load_LRM_database] Loading FANTOM5 (human) from bundled package data ...
#> [load_LRM_database] FANTOM5 (human): 2557 unique LR pairs loaded.
lrm.rat <- load_LRM_database("fantom5", species = "rat")
#> [load_LRM_database] Loading FANTOM5 (rat) from bundled package data ...
#> [load_LRM_database] FANTOM5 (rat): 2557 unique LR pairs loaded.

# User-supplied table -- species argument is ignored. Column names are
# remapped to canonical "ligand" / "receptor".
my.db <- data.frame(
  Ligand   = c("MIF", "VEGFA", "Cxcl12_Pf4"),
  Receptor = c("CD74", "KDR",  "Ackr3")
)
lrm.user <- load_LRM_database(my.db,
                              ligand.col   = "Ligand",
                              receptor.col = "Receptor")
#> [load_LRM_database] Custom table: 3 LR pairs loaded.
# }

# OmniPath needs internet access, so this runs in interactive sessions only.
if (interactive()) {
  lrm.op <- load_LRM_database("omnipath", species = "mouse")
}
